questions.question: What is mixed-media art?
choices: An artwork combining more than one material or process
A work using only one pencil
A print made from a single plate
A digital image with no layers

questions.question: What should an artist consider before combining materials?
choices: Whether all materials have the same color
How they adhere, layer, age, and interact safely
Whether the artwork uses one subject

questions.question: Why create a small material test before a large mixed-media work?
choices: To check compatibility, texture, and appearance

questions.question: What is collage?
choices: An artwork made by assembling attached images or materials

questions.question: How can layering contribute to a mixed-media composition?
choices: It creates depth and relationships among materials
It guarantees the materials will bond
It limits the work to one process

questions.question: Why should adhesives and coatings be chosen carefully?
choices: Every adhesive works on every surface
Some materials may react, detach, or require safe handling
The choice changes only the title

questions.question: What is an assemblage?
choices: A drawing made only with contour lines
A three-dimensional artwork assembled from found or constructed objects

questions.question: A paper collage is curling away from its support. What should the artist investigate?
choices: Adhesive suitability, paper weight, and mounting method

questions.question: How can repetition unify a work made from many materials?
choices: Recurring shapes, colors, or textures can connect different parts
It removes the need for composition

questions.question: What is a found object in art?
choices: A tool made only for painting
An existing object selected and incorporated into an artwork

questions.question: Why document the materials used in an artwork?
choices: It supports reflection, care, and future understanding of the work
It removes the need for safety

questions.question: How can an artist make a fragile material safer to display?
choices: Use suitable support and consider protective mounting

questions.question: What can contrast between rough and smooth surfaces add?
Why might an artist preserve visible seams or edges in collage?
choices: They prove the work is unfinished
They can communicate process and material relationships

questions.question: What does composition organize in a mixed-media piece?
choices: The chemical formula of every material
The placement and relationships of visual elements

questions.question: How can a limited set of materials strengthen a project?
choices: It ensures the artwork is realistic
Constraints can encourage intentional choices and visual unity

questions.question: What is an important safety practice when cutting or assembling materials?
choices: Use tools as instructed and protect the workspace and hands
Cut toward the body for control

questions.question: A project contains many unrelated objects but feels unclear. What revision could help?
choices: Choose a focal idea and arrange materials to support it

questions.question: Why is experimentation valuable in mixed-media art?
choices: Unexpected material interactions can produce new visual possibilities

questions.question: How can an artist make a mixed-media work more accessible to viewers?
choices: Assume every surface can be touched
Provide clear labels or descriptions when materials or meaning need context
